newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police arrest German colony leader Hopp.
newsitem.headline: Chile police arrest German colony leader Hopp.

text.p: Chilean police on Friday arrested one of the leaders of a mysterious German colony when he returned to the country from Argentina with four other settlers.
Police detained Hartmut Hopp, the settlement's spokesman, on his arrival at Santiago's international airport on a flight from the Argentine city of Mendoza, where he had travelled on Thursday.

Hours earlier, a Chilean judge issued arrest warrants against Hopp and his wife, Dorothea Witthahn, after they failed to attend a court hearing on Thursday into charges that they illegally adopted their teenage son Michael. The warrants were issued by Jorge Norambuena, judge at the court in the town of Parral 200 miles (320 km) south of Santiago.
Hopp rejected the allegations made by the teenager's Chilean biological mother, saying the judge's arrest order was illegal.
"It is an invention and is completely without foundation," Hopp told reporters waiting at the airport.

The couple flew to Mendoza accompanied by their son and Rebeca Schaefer, the daughter of the enclave's fugitive founder Paul Schaefer who has been accused of sexually molesting boys at Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony).

Norambuena issued an international arrest warrant last year against the 76-year-old Schaefer but police have been unable to detain the him despite carrying out numerous raids in recent months at the colony of scenic farms and traditional Bavarian houses.
Several hours after Hopp's arrival, two young fugitives who escaped from the settlement last week boarded a flight to Frankfurt accompanied by officials from the German embassy.

The men, 24-year old German Tobias Muller and Chilean Gonzalo Luna, gave evidence on Thursday to another judge in Parral, Hernan Gonzalez, who is investigating claims that Schaefer abused at least five boys at the colony's boarding school.
Local media reported that they told the judge that Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, is hiding in the heavily guarded enclave that he founded in 1961.

Defectors from the colony say residents are not allowed to read newspapers or watch television, their mail is censored, youngsters are drugged and given unusual punishments by Schaefer who does not allow any dissent to his rule.
"The situation within the colony is negative and totally unacceptable. It is a state within a state," said Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco.

A former Protestant preacher and charismatic speaker, Schaefer has been accused of assaulting boys at Colonia Dignidad since 1966. Media reports say he fled Germany in around 1957 after charges of fondling youngsters at an orphange he founded in Bonn.
